summary.title: Being good isn't enough
summary.one_liner: Technical skill alone stops differentiating you as you grow, so combine it with product thinking, project execution and people skills, using feedback, humility and agency to improve.
keywords: how to increase impact at work
why technical skill is not enough for promotion
how to find your weaknesses at work
takeaways: Technical skill is the baseline, but it stops setting you apart as colleagues become equally strong.
Four disciplines show up everywhere: technical skill, product thinking, project execution, and people skills.
Feedback and humility together reveal your weakest discipline and let you act on it.
Agency matters most: take initiative, mentor and be mentored, lead or propose projects, and make your work visible.
summary.summary: This short essay argues that good technical work is necessary but not sufficient for career progress. It proposes four disciplines (technical skill, product thinking, project execution, and people skills) that become more important as you grow more senior. The author recommends finding your weakest discipline through feedback, approaching it with humility, and taking high-agency actions such as mentoring, leading projects, and doing work in the open. The page ends with two recommended books: The Staff Engineer's Path and Thanks for the Feedback.
